topic: Trimming heavy, theatrical exposition into a single silence on the script page
caption:
We talk too much in our films. 

This was three paragraphs of heavy, theatrical exposition explaining a character’s guilt. I crossed it all out for a single, quiet beat: he just stares at the unlit cigarette. When the camera is right in an actor’s face, you don't need them to announce their heartbreak. Trust the silence. 

Writers—how do you know when to kill a line and let the subtext do the work?
